raw_response:
I'm 56, been on this land for 30 years. Never went to school, can't read the bags, but I know my fields. My family has six mouths. Two of my children work in the garment factory over in Handan and send home maybe two thousand yuan a month together. That money helps with the grandchildren's school fees, but I can't use it for the farm — they worked hard for it. The farm has to pay for itself.

I have 10.9 mu. I put 7 mu in wheat-maize, same as always. The other 3.9 mu I plant cotton. The cotton has to go in now — it's almost the end of April, and if I wait too long the season gets short.

For the cotton, I'll plow once with the small tractor my nephew drives. He charges me 30 yuan per mu, but what can I do? I don't have my own machine. I put one bag of compound fertilizer per mu before planting, spread it by hand. When the cotton flowers in July, I'll spread another half bag of urea if the plants look hungry. I water twice from the well — water costs money now, they meter it, so I don't waste it. For bugs, I'll spray three times: once for weeds, twice for insects. Cotton gets bollworms bad if you don't watch. I hire five day-laborers for picking season because my back hurts and the children can't get leave from the factory. I expect about 230 kg of lint per mu if the weather holds. Last year was a little less because of the dry spell.

The wheat went in last October. I gave it base fertilizer then — one bag of compound and some urea per mu, spread before planting. Now it's April, the wheat is jointing. I'll put another half bag of urea per mu this week while the weather is warm. I irrigate two more times before June harvest — once now at jointing, once when the ears come out. The well water is expensive, so I don't water like the big farms do. I expect about 400 kg per mu. My neighbor Auntie Li got 450 kg last year, but her son bought her that fancy fertilizer and I can't afford that.

The maize goes in right after wheat harvest in mid-June. There's no time — maybe three days between cutting wheat and planting maize. I'll rotary till quick and plant. I buy new hybrid seed every year for maize, saved seed doesn't work for hybrids, it grows short and strange. One bag of compound fertilizer at planting per mu, and if the leaves look yellow at the big flare stage I'll topdress a little urea. Water it once or twice, depending on rain. Maize usually gives me about 420 kg per mu.

September will be tight — cotton picking and maize harvest at the same time. The maize can wait a week in the field if it has to, but cotton can't wait or the bolls open and the cotton gets dirty. So I'll hire a combine for the maize and focus family labor on cotton.

Fertilizer is expensive this year, so I'm not putting more than usual. I'd rather get a little less yield than have no cash for medicine if someone gets sick. That's how I think — safe, not sorry.
